- Position 0 (w) → gets color from position 19 (S)? No, w→g
- Actually let me check: position 0 was w, now g. Position 1 was g, now S. Position 2 was S, now b...
- So position i gets the color from position i-1 (counter-clockwise shift)
- Position 0 (w) → g (from position 1)
- Position 1 (g) → S (from position 2)
- Position 2 (S) → b (from position 3)
...
- Position 19 (S) → w (from position 0)
Wait, that's a counter-clockwise rotation: each position gets the color from the next position clockwise.
But positions 20 (R) and 21 (N) stayed the same. So the red and green shapes are fixed anchors, and clicking the red shape rotates all other colors counter-clockwise by one position.
Actually wait, let me re-check. The red shape at position 20 stayed R, and the green at position 21 stayed N. But all other positions shifted. So the cycle is:
- Colors flow counter-clockwise around the frame
- The red and green shapes are fixed and don't participate in the rotation
Hmm, but that doesn't quite work either because the colors don't just skip R and N - they seem to flow through the entire ring.
Let me reconsider. Maybe the red and green shapes ARE part of the cycle, but they're special because they're larger (40 pixels vs 16). When I click the red shape, it triggers a rotation.

- Node 26 (R, 40px) → now b, 16px (became a regular blue block)
- Node 27 (N, 40px) → now R, 40px (became the red shape)
- Node 28 (p, 16px) → now N, 40px (became the green shape)
So the red shape moved from position 20 to position 21, and the green shape moved from position 21 to position 28 (which is the left_mid position). The colors shifted along with the shapes.

Actually, looking at the after ASCII:
- R31: cR6c4S4c32S4c4N6c2
So R is at col 1-6 and N is at col 54-59. That's the same positions as before.
But the node data says node 26 changed from R to b, and node 27 changed from N to R, and node 28 changed from p to N. This is confusing because the node IDs are assigned by position (top-most, left-most), so the IDs shift as objects move.
Let me re-think. The key insight is that clicking on the red shape caused a rotation of all colors around the frame. The red shape itself seems to stay in place (or maybe it's the anchor point).

The fact that there are 8 blue blocks in the top bar (node 1) suggests there might be 8 steps or 8 positions to reach.

Actually, let me first understand the initial state better. The original state had:
- Top: w, g, S, b, p, Y, g
- Left: S, p, g
- Right: p, b, S
- Bottom: w, w, b, b, S, p, g

- Mid-right: N (green shape)
After one click on red:

- Right: b, S, g
- Bottom: g, w, w, b, b, S, p
